draft.title: Water on Earth
card: Water exists in all three states at Earth's surface. It is solid as ice and snow, liquid in oceans, rivers and groundwater, and gas as water vapour in the air.
Most of Earth's water is in the oceans. Ocean water is salty, so it is not fit to drink without treatment.
Only a small share of Earth's water is fresh water, which has very little dissolved salt.
Much of that fresh water is locked up as ice in glaciers and ice sheets. Only a small part is liquid water in rivers, lakes and groundwater that people can reach and drink.
draft.remember: Water is plentiful on Earth, but drinkable fresh water is only a small share.

a.q: Why is most of the water on Earth not fit to drink?
opts: It is mostly salty ocean water
It is mostly water vapour in the air
It is mostly polluted river water
It is mostly groundwater deep underground
a.why: Most of Earth's water is in the oceans, and ocean water is salty. Groundwater can be fresh, and only a small share of all water is vapour in the air.
a.clue: Think about where most of the water is stored.

b.q: Mia sees that a large share of Earth's fresh water is frozen in glaciers. What does this mean for drinking water?
opts: Much fresh water is not easy for people to reach
Fresh water cannot exist as a liquid
Glacier ice is salty and cannot be drunk
Most fresh water is found in the oceans
b.why: Fresh water locked in ice sheets and glaciers is hard to reach, so the supply people can use is smaller than the total fresh water. It is not salty, and fresh water does exist as a liquid in rivers, lakes and groundwater.
b.clue: Fresh and easy to reach are not the same thing.

a.best: It is mostly salty ocean water

b.best: Much fresh water is not easy for people to reach
